A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Memory-R1 and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The method and retained experiments can be matched across versions, including relocated figures and implementation details. v5 adds Appendix G.

before.justification: v4 reports original benchmark evaluations on LoCoMo, MSC, and LongMemEval, together with component ablations, training curves, and case studies in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains the original empirical evaluations and adds baseline comparisons and inference-latency measurements in Figure 8, Table 5, and Appendix G.

M1.justification: Algorithm 3 changes UPDATE from simply adding merged memories to removing the retrieved old entries before inserting their replacements. This is a limited correction to the stated procedure; the architecture, distillation policy, and RL objectives remain unchanged. Algorithm 5 retains the union-only update, so a corresponding implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: Both versions train on LoCoMo and evaluate the same LoCoMo, MSC, and LongMemEval tasks. The new comparisons and latency analyses do not introduce documented dataset or task coverage. Appendix B.1 drops the LongMemEval oracle specification without identifying a replacement scenario; this does not establish a coverage change.

E2.justification: Table 1 replaces Zep with MemoryOS for both backbones. LongMemEval comparison membership expands beyond the retained Base/PPO/GRPO results: new Table 5 evaluates LoCoMo (RAG), A-Mem, Mem0, and Memory-SFT. Figure 8 also introduces an evaluated Base + Reranker comparator. Together these substantially expand the comparison evidence.

E3.justification: v5 introduces latency evaluation using median (p50) and tail (p95) inference time, including separate measurements for Memory Manager, Memory Search, and Answer Agent across two backbones. The existing accuracy metrics, stated 152/81/1307 split, model sizes, decoding settings, and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 and Figure 8 add a comparison testing learned memory distillation against reranking on accuracy and latency. Appendix G adds systematic component-level efficiency analyses across Base, PPO, and GRPO on two backbones. The original component-ablation graphic, reward analysis, stronger-manager comparison, and appendix case studies are retained; revised ablation prose should not be mistaken for newly performed ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new p50/p95 values summarize inference-latency distributions as performance metrics; they are not confidence intervals or uncertainty estimates for the reported accuracy.

E6.justification: v5 adds MemoryOS scores, removes Zep scores, and adds LongMemEval baseline and latency results. Table 5 repeats the previously reported PPO/GRPO LongMemEval totals alongside new comparators. Retained Table 1 method scores and Tables 2–4 are unchanged; for example, LLaMA GRPO overall F1/B1/J remains 45.02/37.51/62.74. Section 4.4 corrects swapped F1/B1 reporting against unchanged Figure 5, while Section 4.2 replaces the relative-gain calculations with comparisons against MemoryOS.

T1.justification: The PPO/GRPO formulations and exact-match reward definitions retain their mathematical substance. Equation 5 standardizes policy notation, and the duplicate Answer Agent reward equation is replaced by equivalent prose. No theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The introduction changes the claimed LLaMA relative gains from 48%/69%/37% to 28%/34%/30% for F1/B1/J. However, it still names Mem0, whereas the revised percentages match MemoryOS in Table 1 and Section 4.2. The central claims about two-agent RL, 152-example training, LoCoMo performance, scaling, and zero-shot transfer remain.

C2.justification: v5 adds interpretations that RL improves inference efficiency, that GRPO encourages more concise reasoning, and that learned distillation offers an accuracy–latency Pareto improvement. These arguments were absent from v4. The existing limitations concerning dialogue-centric evaluation, multimodal extension, and separate agent training remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 removes the explicit statement that the oracle version of LongMemEval was used, reducing reproducibility information without documenting a replacement setting. Implementation details formerly in Section 4.1 are consolidated into Appendix D; their hardware, learning rates, batch sizes, token limits, and framework information are retained. The new reranker comparison does not identify its reranker model.

R1.justification: v5 adds the MemoryOS citation and description, removes Zep and the Sulemani CRUD reference, and revises ReadAgent's description to emphasize gist memory for long contexts. ReadAgent and MemoryBank remain identifiable as the previously discussed systems despite bibliography corrections. The broader positioning of Memory-R1 as an RL approach to memory management is retained.

P1.justification: v5 condenses the experimental setup and conclusion, rewrites component-ablation explanations, consolidates implementation prose into Appendix D, and adds Appendix G. It also makes localized wording, reference, and author-list edits. The overall narrative and main section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v5 substantially expands the visual evidence with the accuracy–latency comparison in Figure 8, component plots in Figures 13–14, and LongMemEval Table 5. Existing scaling, generalization, and ablation figures are relocated, and the training-curve and stronger-manager figures exchange numbering. All seven original graphical figures retain their image content; the visual expansion comes from the new displays.

improvement.justification: v5 corrects several metric-attribution and percentage errors and adds useful baseline and efficiency evidence. However, it removes the LongMemEval oracle disclosure, attaches revised introduction gains to the wrong comparator, and introduces unexplained accuracy discrepancies in Figure 13: LLaMA GRPO F1 is about 35.7 there versus 45.02 overall in Table 1 and Figure 8. These changes improve parts of the empirical account while weakening transparency and consistency elsewhere. The PDFs do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
